newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY FORINT ENDS FIRMER AGAINST THE DOLLAR.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY FORINT ENDS FIRMER AGAINST THE DOLLAR.

text.p: Hungary's forint closed slightly firmer against the dollar on Monday, tracking the movements of the dollar/mark on international markets, some 30 pips below the central bank's resistance level, dealers said.
"(The forint) moved with the dollar/mark", said Robert Szucs of Creditanstalt Rt.
The forint finished at 174.95/175.00, compared with 175.03/08 at midday and 175.05/15 at the opening.
Dealers said the National Bank of Hungary's (NBH) repo rate cuts came too late in the afternoon to influence the interbank foreign currency market.
"And the NBH only followed what had happened on the market," said Unicbank's Gabor Butor. "Government securities yields are coming down, it is clear that short-term rates must follow them too."
Buying interest for foreign currencies was slightly larger than for forints as Hungary's declining interest rates made the forint decreasingly attractive in the past few months, dealers said.
"The banks keep long forint (positions) only for the sake of keeping up liquidity," Butor said.
The Swiss frank was in focus in futures trade on the Budapest Commodity Exchange. The Swiss frank eased or remained steady, while all dollar maturities went up by between 0.49 and 0.61 forints.
